replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: I remember enjoying some of it when I was younger, especially basic arithmetic and geometry. But after lower secondary school, I didn’t pursue math much beyond that. My father had a PhD in physics, so he always talked about equations and formulas, but I never really got into the deeper parts. Now, I use math occasionally for budgeting and cooking, which is helpful.

replies.How would you explain, step by step, how: First, write the equation in standard form: ax² + bx + c = 0. Then use the quadratic formula: x equals negative b plus or minus square root of b squared minus four ac all over two a. Plug in your values and calculate each part. You’ll get two solutions, which are the roots of the equation.

To find stationary points, take the derivative of f(x), call it f'(x). Set f'(x) equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are where the slope is zero. Plug each back into the original function to get the corresponding y-value. Those (x,y) pairs are your stationary points.
